intro.name: The problem
intro.text:
The village's researchers have been arguing for days. Apparently, there is a problem so complicated that even the most learned villagers cannot agree on the answer.
Some believe it is a matter of mathematics. Others insist that it is a problem of engineering. One particularly stubborn researcher believes that the entire problem is nonsense.
At last, (researcher1) and (researcher2) agree to settle the matter with a competition. {@Chief} has offered {a generous prize|a handsome trophy|a lifetime supply of writing materials|a rather impressive coconut} to whoever can find the best solution.
The problem is... {A}.

ask.name: What to encourage
ask.text:
(Researcher1) is {B}, while (researcher2) is {B2}. They have until sundown to present their work.
What should the village encourage?

indep.text: The two researchers separate their materials and get to work. (Researcher1) {fills several pages with calculations|builds a miniature model|draws a complicated diagram|stares at the problem for hours}. Meanwhile, (researcher2) {tries a completely different method|consults old records|makes measurements in the field|starts over twice}.

demo.text: {@Chief} declares that a solution is only useful if the village can understand how it works. The researchers must explain their reasoning and demonstrate their ideas before the judges. One researcher looks delighted. The other looks as though (otherr.he/she) would rather face a swarm of bees.

collab.text: Perhaps the researchers are wasting time trying to defeat each other. {@Chief} suggests that they work together instead. (Researcher1) {agrees immediately|hesitates|looks offended}. (Researcher2) {smiles|grumbles|asks whether the prize will be shared}.

drew.item: determining how to build a bridge across a ravine without wasting wood

i1.text: Both researchers arrive at the same correct answer by entirely different methods. They argue over whose method is more elegant, then reluctantly admit that both are useful.

i2.text: (Researcher1) produces a brilliant solution but cannot explain it clearly. (Researcher2) gives a less impressive answer with a wonderful explanation. The judges must decide what matters most.

i3.text: One researcher discovers a tiny error in the other's calculations. The embarrassed competitor corrects it, then finds a flaw in the first researcher's model. Neither gets to feel superior for long.

i4.text: Both researchers confidently present the WRONG answer. A child points out that they have forgotten to account for the weight of the bridge itself. The researchers stare at each other in horror.

i5.text: The researchers solve different parts of the problem. Neither can finish alone, but their combined work provides the answer.

i6.text: Both researchers run out of time. {@Chief} awards no prize, but asks them to continue their work tomorrow.

d1.text: The model works perfectly! The audience applauds. The researchers are {overjoyed|relieved|astonished that nobody noticed the glue}.

d2.text: The model collapses before anyone touches it. A very awkward silence follows. The researchers agree to investigate what went wrong.

text_only.reason: a model, not a village structure: nothing is damaged

d3.text: The explanation is so complicated that the judges fall asleep. The design is sound, but someone must translate it into language ordinary villagers can understand.

d4.text: A spectator asks a simple question that neither researcher considered. They return to their calculations, embarrassed but grateful.

d5.text: The demonstration works, but only because a child has been holding up the model from behind the table. The judges demand a fair retest.

d6.text: The researchers discover that their supposedly ancient measurement was taken using a bent stick. They agree to start over.

c1.text: After a few disagreements, the researchers combine their ideas into a design neither could have produced alone.

c2.text: They spend the entire afternoon arguing about who gets to hold the measuring stick. No solution is reached.

c3.text: (Researcher1) discovers the theory, while (researcher2) develops a practical method. They share the prize and celebrate quietly.

c4.text: The collaboration reveals that the problem was based on a false assumption. The researchers explain this to {@chief}, who is {impressed|disappointed|secretly relieved}.

c5.text: The two become close friends and continue working together. Their next project is already causing arguments.

j2.text: (Researcher2) wins for elegance and clarity. (Researcher1) demands to see the scoring rubric.

j3.text: The judges declare a tie. Both researchers are delighted - until they realize they must share the trophy.

j4.text: The judges award the prize to the child who spotted the crucial mistake. The researchers {laugh|applaud|look deeply embarrassed}.

j5.text: No winner is declared because both solutions are useful in different circumstances.

argue.name: What counts
argue.text:
The judges cannot agree whether the best solution should be {the most accurate|the easiest to explain|the cheapest to build|the safest|the most elegant|the quickest to carry out}.
After a long discussion, they {publish a set of standards for future competitions|ask the villagers to vote|award a joint victory|postpone the decision until the designs are tested}.
(Researcher1) and (researcher2) learn that solving a problem is not always the same as deciding which solution is best.

childobs.name: The child
childobs.text:
A young villager, (child), quietly asks, "But what about {the weight of the bridge|the missing corner|the extra support|the water that leaks out|the shadow on the other side}?"
The researchers freeze.
Apparently, the answer was sitting right in front of them.
(Researcher1) {laughs at (researcher1.himself/herself)|thanks the child|offers to teach (child.him/her) more mathematics}. (Researcher2) {looks mortified|congratulates the child|immediately begins checking every other calculation}.
The researchers return to work.

q1.name: A quiet failure
q1.text:
By sundown, the problem remains unsolved. Nobody has won the prize. The researchers pack away their tools, tired and disappointed.
Still, the village now knows more about the problem than it did yesterday. Perhaps that is progress enough for one day.
